Independently re-scanned all 20 verses of Psalm 147 (letters-only endswith check on every token, verse_map_oshb.json): tokens ending in the nun-vav string occur at exactly 3 verses / 4 tokens -- אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (147:1), אֲדוֹנֵ֣ינוּ (147:5), and BOTH עֱנ֣וּ and לֵאלֹהֵ֣ינוּ (147:7) -- of which עֱנ֣וּ is the 2mp imperative 'answer/sing,' not a 1cp pronominal-suffix noun; only 3 of the 4 are genuine 1cp elements, and NONE is a cohortative (1cp prefix-conjugation) verb. Zero cohortative forms confirmed by direct scan of every verse in the psalm. The claim that Ps 147 outside 147:12 is 'otherwise third-person description or first-person-plural summons' is confirmed false as written: it omits the two 2mp imperatives at 147:1 and 147:7 and asserts a mood (1cp summons) that does not occur anywhere in the psalm.

Independently re-derived the same census: nun-vav-ending tokens = 4 over 3 verses (147:1, 147:5, 147:7x2), nun-initial tokens = 4 over 3 verses (נָ֝עִים, נָאוָ֥ה at 147:1; נִדְחֵ֖י at 147:2; נוֹתֵ֣ן at 147:9) -- two adjectives, a construct noun, and a participle, zero 1cp imperfects. The row's genuinely proprietary fact is the 2fs-suffix addressee run confined to 147:12-14 (independently re-verified below, OL-487-1 adjudication) -- not the mood contrast as stated.

peer_findings.claim: citation_sweep.py's Hebrew-quote-binding arm (lesson-j collate arm) accepts tier 'nfd' as passing for POINTED Hebrew runs, contradicting its own docstring and TOOLKIT.md's statement that only byte tier is quotation-grade for pointed text -- this is why rows 490, 491, and 492 all passed citation_sweep.py GREEN despite carrying nfd-degraded pointed quotes.
peer_findings.evidence: Source-read confirmation, tools/citation_sweep.py, the walk() closure's quote-binding check: 'if (tier in ("byte", "nfd")) if pointed else tier != "none":' -- nfd is accepted for pointed runs. Independently re-ran citation_sweep.py against all 9 rows in this batch: GREEN, 0 problems, despite 5 confirmed nfd-tier pointed quotes located across rows 490/491/492 by direct collate.py re-derivation. This corroborates the same toolkit-gap observation both OL-490-1 and OL-492-1 note in passing (not filed as a row challenge in either case); recorded here as a campaign-level (not row-level) finding since it affects every future row the tool screens, not only this batch's rows.
